metadata.name: WalkSafe-AI Bogota ZAT profiles
metadata.extent: Bogota D.C. Zones with no analysis data in any table lie outside the city, in the greater metropolitan area, and are not rendered.
metadata.description: Bogota D.C. transport analysis zones, 2019 vintage, joined to cluster profiles from a DINO/STRIDE extraction of 27 built-environment features over ~312,000 Google Street View prediction points, and to 2015-2019 crash counts.
metadata.caveat: ECOLOGICAL. These are area-level associations across Bogota D.C. ZAT zones, not individual risk. A zone's colour describes the zone, not the people in it.
metadata.taxonomy_note: The 27 features derive from the CANVAS pedestrian safety audit instrument, which also seeded the Gemini taxonomy in scoring/prompts.py. They are not independent instruments.

crash_outcomes.damage_note: Damage-only crashes are excluded. Nearly every pedestrian struck by a motor vehicle is injured or killed, and the source data agree: 19 damage-only crashes across all 783 zones with crash data. The source `total` column (injury + death + damage) is not carried; use `casualties`.

cluster_rr.note: Reference is cluster 4: the dense arterial / mass-transit corridor profile, highest on every infrastructure count and highest crash burden. Clusters 1-3 are protective relative to it.
cluster_rr.age_note: The Bogota models were fitted across all age groups. 'replication' (n = 770) is that primary result. 'plus_pct60' (n = 768) additionally adjusts for the ZAT-level 60+ population share, and exists to support comparison with the Philadelphia older-adult focus. The 60+ share is a zone-level covariate, not an age-stratified outcome — these are not older-adult-specific risks. The two specifications are not interchangeable; do not mix estimates across them.

exposure.definition: walking and public-transport trips to each zone recorded by the 2019 Bogota mobility survey, a one-day travel diary of a representative sample from every ZAT (Encuesta de Movilidad)
exposure.note: Outcome per 10,000 trips. This is the exposure offset used in Zewdie et al. 2024 for the ZAT tree analysis; the per-km2 fields remain as area densities and are not exposure-adjusted.
